Our Mission

Built on Service,
Driven by Knowledge

Patriot Scholar Press exists to publish books that matter — works of practical wisdom, academic rigor, and patriotic conviction that help Americans of all ages navigate life with purpose and clarity.

Founded in New Braunfels, Texas in 2026, Patriot Scholar Press is an imprint of MJHW Holdings, LLC. We believe that education and service to country are not competing values — they are the same value, expressed differently.

From practical guides for young adults stepping into the world after high school to scholarly works on law enforcement, leadership, and American civic life — every title we publish carries a message worth passing on.

About Dr. Watts

Dr. John Harrison Watts, PhD

“Your limitations don’t define you — your drive does.”

Dr. John Harrison Watts has lived the American Dream in every sense. A decorated police officer, U.S. Army soldier, Texas State Guard Chief Warrant Officer 4 (CW4), university professor, city commissioner, and entrepreneur — Dr. Watts brings a uniquely multidimensional perspective to everything he writes and every stage he graces.

He holds a PhD and has spent his career not only serving his community but mentoring the next generation of scholars, leaders, and patriots through the McNair Scholars Program and graduate education. He is the founder of The Conflict Ref, LLC, and the driving intellectual force behind Patriot Scholar Press.

Dr. Watts’s published works span practical life guidance, criminal justice scholarship, and legal studies — a body of work that reflects the full range of his service and expertise. He resides in Texas, where he continues to teach, write, mentor, and chase a few dreams of his own.

About the Author

Cristina Moreno-Garcia

Author · Journalist · Yoga Teacher

“The next version of you starts today.”

Cristina Moreno-Garcia is a bilingual and bicultural journalist, marketing and communications specialist, and certified yoga teacher who has spent her career helping other people tell their stories. Aging Boldly is her first book under her own name.

Born and raised in Mexico, Cristina began her career writing for El Norte and Reforma Newspapers (Monterrey, Mexico) before moving to the United States and reinventing herself in nonprofit marketing. She completed her MBA at Our Lady of the Lake University in San Antonio, where she studied Applied Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Business, a curriculum that was the motivation for this book.

Cristina is certified in Hatha yoga, Stronger Yoga, Yoga for Sciatica, Mat Pilates, and Coaching Women Into and Beyond Menopause. She teaches and coaches with a particular focus on midlife women navigating perimenopause, hormonal change, and the kind of reinvention that nobody warns you about in your twenties.

She writes about wellness, self-care, and the absurd small daily questions of being a woman at her blog, soselfie.com.

Cristina lives in San Antonio, Texas, with her husband Eduardo, and has a great relationship with her three grown stepchildren, Naty, Bianca, and Diego. She is five-foot-two, blonde by decision, and a size 4 with a particular weakness for platforms, fashion, and any gadget releases. She volunteers at the McNay Art Museum in San Antonio and travels often to Monterrey to visit family and friends.

This is her first book, but not the last… She is currently working on her first fiction story.

About the Author

Stacey Parker

Hey! I’m Stacey P.! I’m a wife, mom, Gigi, and a 55-year-old woman who is absolutely convinced there’s still a teenage girl living inside me!

I love the beach, anything that sparkles, and finding reasons to laugh. I love big, treasure my family, and believe some of the best moments in life are the ones you never planned.

I’ve made unforgettable memories, had my share of adventures, and collected a few stories that are probably better left untold!

At 55, I’m enjoying life, embracing who I am, and realizing that some of the best surprises come when you least expect them.

Like becoming an author! What started as one crazy little idea has taken me completely outside my comfort zone. Never in a million years did I imagine I’d be doing something like this, but here I am!

And maybe that’s the most exciting part. I get to share a little piece of myself with the world, hopefully make someone smile along the way, and discover what else I might be capable of.

Who knows what I’ll dream up next?

About the Author

Shirley “Shoo Shoo” Power Watts

Shirley “Shoo Shoo” Watts has spent 83 years collecting stories, learning life’s lessons, building a family, and discovering that some of the greatest wisdom comes from life’s simplest experiences.

Born and raised in Dallas, Texas, Shirley grew up in a modest household with her mother, Clemmie, and older sister, Janette. Raised by a hardworking single mother during a time when money was scarce, Shirley learned early the importance of faith, determination, independence, and making the most of every opportunity.

Her beloved nickname, “Shoo Shoo,” came from her young nephew Donnie, who couldn’t quite pronounce Shirley. He called her “Shoo,” and before long, the name became “Shoo Shoo.” It stuck, becoming a name cherished by generations of family and friends.

Shirley’s life has been anything but ordinary. She began working as a teenager and collected experiences that sound as though they belong in a Hollywood movie. While working at the Majestic Theatre in Dallas, she met Elvis Presley during his military service at Fort Hood. She once danced with legendary actor John Wayne at a party and even flew Braniff Airlines’ top stewardess to Acapulco. These are just a few of the extraordinary memories woven into her remarkable life.

But Shirley’s greatest accomplishments have never been about the famous people she met or the places she traveled. They have been about the life she built and the family she raised.

As the mother of two sons, Shirley watched one become a college professor and author, while the other built a successful career with UPS and developed an extensive real estate business in Vernon, Texas. She has been a small business owner, enjoyed a career with the Texas A&M Extension Service, and continues to operate her own real estate company at the age of 83. Retirement, it seems, has never been part of Shoo Shoo’s vocabulary.

A born-again Christian, Shirley draws her strength, perspective, and inspiration from her faith. She believes that life’s challenges offer opportunities to grow, that good decisions are grounded in sound principles, and that experience is one of life’s greatest teachers.

Today, Shirley is the beloved matriarch of the Watts family. Whether offering advice, sharing a story, or helping someone navigate a difficult decision, Shoo Shoo has become a trusted source of wisdom for family and friends. When people need guidance, they know whom to call.

When she isn’t managing her real estate business or spending time with family, Shirley enjoys quilting, traveling with her girlfriends, and making new memories to add to her already remarkable collection.

In Shoo Shoo’s Rules, Shirley shares 20 guiding principles developed through eight decades of living, learning, loving, succeeding, and occasionally making mistakes. Each rule is accompanied by a personal experience that brings its lesson to life, offering readers practical wisdom to help them make better decisions and navigate their own journeys.

For Shirley, writing this book is about something much greater than sharing advice. It is about leaving a legacy.

She hopes that long after she is gone, her children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and even descendants not yet born will open the pages of her book and discover the woman their family lovingly called Shoo Shoo. Through her stories, her faith, her humor, and her wisdom, they will have the opportunity to know her, learn from her, and carry her lessons into generations yet to come.

Because some of life’s greatest lessons are worth passing down, and some legacies deserve to live forever.

About the Author

Cynthia Duckworth

Cynthia was born and raised in Green, a growing city in Northeast Ohio. She is married to her high school sweetheart, Jim. They have four beautiful daughters, Marinna, Cierra, and twins Savannah and Julianna. Marinna was born with severe special needs and died at the age of 14. Cierra, Savannah and Julianna live a few houses up from Jim and Cynthia.

Jim and Cynthia accepted Christ after Cierra was born, and she strives to glorify Christ in all she does. Cynthia has a calling for counseling. She was going to counseling before Marinna died, and the counselor said there was really nothing she could offer as Cynthia’s depression was situational and nothing was going to change until Marinna died. She left the office feeling so hopeless and just before she reached her car she stopped and realized she always had hope in Christ. Cynthia never wanted anyone to feel like that again and in that devastating moment, a passion for counseling was born. She feels strongly that her role was not as a licensed counselor but more in a ministry capacity. She worked in the mental health field for many years before an early retirement due to health issues. Cynthia has earned a bachelor’s degree in Business Management from Malone University, and a master’s degree in Pastoral Counseling from Liberty Baptist Theological Seminary. She is half way through her doctorate in Community Care and Counseling with a focus on traumatology from Liberty University. Cynthia is a Certified Intuitive Eating Counselor, a licensed Be Body Positive Facilitator, and a Board Certified Christian Counselor. She served as a volunteer parent mentor for the local Children’s hospital for 15 years helping other parents with special needs children navigate all the challenges involved in raising a special needs child.

Cynthia was an active volunteer with Civil Air Patrol, the official auxiliary of the United States Air Force for many years. She earned several awards including the USAF Organizational Excellence Ribbon, the Meritorious Service Award, and the Life Saving Award. She commanded a Composite Squadron and was the Ohio Wing Encampment Commander for 2013. She was proud to be part of the team that led her unit’s cadet color guard to the regional competition three years in a row after winning the Ohio Wing Competition each year. She volunteered for many other activities including several Ohio Wing encampments, Ohio Wing Annual Award and NCSA Board, Air Shows, Cyber Patriot Coach, and was a dedicated Cadet Programs Officer. Cynthia brought Civil Air Patrol to the Ohio Public Schools and commanded the first school based squadron in the state of Ohio.

Cynthia has had a passion for leadership since her high school days in AFJROTC. She developed and taught leadership classes in the public school system for many years. She taught leadership classes in Civil Air Patrol to cadets and senior members. Cynthia is always learning and working to improve her leadership skills and loves to help others develop into effective servant leadership. Look for a book on servant leadership in the future!

Cynthia’s first book, Who Am I? Discovering your identity in Christ, will be available soon.

Cynthia is an accomplished public speaker and is happy to discuss opportunities.

About the Author

Lt. Col. Mary Jo Watts

USAF, NC · Retired

Mary Jo Watts has lived a life defined by faith, family, service, and a willingness to step forward when others need help.

Raised in Green, Ohio, as the middle child of seven children, Mary Jo grew up in a large Catholic family where life offered plenty of opportunities to learn about responsibility, relationships, and finding her own place in the world. Her journey would eventually take her far beyond Ohio, into military service, the operating room, business ownership, and humanitarian efforts around the world.

Although raised Catholic, Mary Jo later embraced the Protestant faith. Throughout the many chapters of her life, her belief in Jesus Christ has remained a source of strength and guidance.

Mary Jo served her country in the United States Air Force, retiring as a Lieutenant Colonel. She also pursued a career in healthcare, becoming a Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (CRNA). Over the years, she built a successful career in anesthesia and established her own healthcare business. Along the way, she learned that success often requires courage, sacrifice, perseverance, and the willingness to make difficult decisions.

But some of Mary Jo’s most meaningful experiences have occurred outside the traditional boundaries of her career.

In 2025, she traveled to Peru on a medical mission to help provide free surgical care to people who otherwise might have gone without treatment. She has also advocated for Afghan interpreters seeking visas to the United States, efforts that earned her recognition through a Yellow Rose of Texas commission from the Governor’s Office. Her continued support of the Vulnerable People Project reflects her commitment to helping individuals who cannot always help themselves.

Through these experiences, Mary Jo has come to understand that service is not limited to wearing a military uniform or practicing medicine. Sometimes it means speaking up for someone without a voice, extending a helping hand, or simply refusing to look away when another person is suffering.

As a wife, mother, and member of a blended family, Mary Jo understands that life’s most important lessons are often learned through relationships, challenges, unexpected turns, and the ordinary moments that become extraordinary memories.

Her memoir is an opportunity to look back on the experiences that shaped her, the people who influenced her, the decisions that changed her direction, and the faith that helped guide her through it all.

Mary Jo does not believe that a meaningful life must be perfect. Rather, it is built through the choices we make, the lessons we learn, the people we love, and the opportunities we take to make a difference.

Through her story, she hopes to share not only what she has accomplished, but what she has learned along the way.

Because in the end, a life well lived is not simply about where we have been or what we have achieved. It is about who we have become and what we leave behind.

For Authors

Publish Your First Book

Turn Your Manuscript Into a Published Book

Have you always dreamed of becoming a published author? Whether you've written a memoir, leadership book, business guide, devotional, military history, or personal story, Patriot Scholar Press is here to help you bring your manuscript to life.

We specialize in helping first-time authors navigate the publishing process from start to finish. Publishing a book can seem overwhelming — but you don't have to do it alone. We'll walk beside you every step of the way.

Your story matters. Let us help you share it with the world.

Pricing

Two Ways to Publish Your Book

Choose the payment option that fits your goals. Both options include our standard publishing package for one book—and you retain ownership of your work.

Option A

Standard Publishing Package

$1,295 total

A straightforward path to preparing and publishing your book.

  • $395 upfront
  • Three monthly payments of $300
  • No interest
  • No ongoing subscription required

Includes publishing consultation, project coordination, interior formatting, cover design coordination, ISBN assignment, Amazon KDP setup, paperback and eBook publication, and launch consultation.

You retain your copyright and receive 100% of royalties paid by distribution platforms.

Ask About Option A

Option B

Publishing & Marketing Partnership

$395 upfront
+ $99 per month for 12 months

Publish your book with smaller monthly payments and continued marketing opportunities through Patriot Scholar Press.

  • Our standard publishing package for one book
  • An author profile and book listing on our website
  • Inclusion in selected Patriot Scholar Press website promotions
  • Opportunities for book display and sales at selected trade shows and events we attend

First-year total: $1,583. A 12-month commitment applies.

Beginning in month 13, your subscription drops to $14.99 per month for continued website marketing and participation in selected trade-show and event opportunities. After the initial commitment, you may cancel future monthly renewals.

Ask About Option B

Part of Option B

Earn From Copies We Purchase

As part of Option B, you agree to supply an initial order of 20 finished books, which Patriot Scholar Press purchases from you at your documented printing cost plus $5 per copy. You earn $100 above printing cost on that initial order.

For example, if printing costs $4 per book, we pay you $9 per copy—a total of $180 for 20 books, with shipping arranged separately.

These books become our inventory for resale through our website and at events. You receive your payment when we purchase the books, rather than waiting for retail sales. Additional orders depend on demand.

Your Book. Your Ownership.

Under either option, you retain ownership of your work and receive all royalties paid to you by publishing platforms. For copies purchased directly by Patriot Scholar Press, your compensation is included in our purchase price; no additional royalty is paid when we resell those copies.

Ready to begin? Email books@patriotscholarpress.com to schedule a discovery conversation.

Packages cover one standard manuscript. Extensive editing, illustrations, hardcover editions, and other custom services are quoted separately. Marketing participation does not guarantee sales or placement at every event. Publication timing depends on manuscript readiness, author approvals, and platform review.
